subject: science
title: The Solar System, Moon and seasons

cards.back: The Sun and everything that orbits it: eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets.
cards.say: Solar System. The Sun and everything that orbits it: eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets.

cards.back: A star at the centre of the Solar System. It gives out light and heat.
cards.say: Sun. A star at the centre of the Solar System. It gives out light and heat.

cards.front: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.
cards.back: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
cards.say: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.. Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

cards.front: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
cards.back: Mercury.
cards.say: Which planet is closest to the Sun? Mercury.

cards.back: Jupiter.
cards.say: Which is the largest planet? Jupiter.

cards.front: Which planets are the four rocky planets?
cards.back: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
cards.say: Which planets are the four rocky planets? Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

cards.back: The large planets Jupiter and Saturn, made mostly of gas.
cards.say: gas giants. The large planets Jupiter and Saturn, made mostly of gas.

cards.back: A region between Mars and Jupiter with many pieces of rock that orbit the Sun.
cards.say: asteroid belt. A region between Mars and Jupiter with many pieces of rock that orbit the Sun.

cards.back: The curved path of one object around another, such as Earth around the Sun.
cards.say: orbit. The curved path of one object around another, such as Earth around the Sun.

cards.front: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun?
cards.back: One year, which is about 365 and a quarter days.
cards.say: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun? One year, which is about three hundred and sixty five and a quarter days.

cards.front: How long does Earth take to rotate once on its axis?
cards.back: About 24 hours, which is one day.
cards.say: How long does Earth take to rotate once on its axis? About twenty four hours, which is one day.

cards.back: Earth spins. The side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night.
cards.say: What causes day and night? Earth spins. The side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night.

cards.front: Does the Moon make its own light?
cards.back: No. It reflects light from the Sun.
cards.say: Does the Moon make its own light? No. It reflects light from the Sun.

cards.front: How long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
cards.back: About 27 days to orbit once. The phases take about 29 and a half days to repeat.
cards.say: How long does the Moon take to orbit Earth? About 27 days to orbit once. The phases take about 29 and a half days to repeat.

cards.front: What causes the phases of the Moon?
cards.back: We see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth.
cards.say: What causes the phases of the Moon? We see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth.

cards.back: The phase when the side of the Moon facing Earth is not lit, so we cannot see it.
cards.say: new Moon. The phase when the side of the Moon facing Earth is not lit, so we cannot see it.

cards.back: The phase when the whole face of the Moon that we see is lit.
cards.say: full Moon. The phase when the whole face of the Moon that we see is lit.

cards.back: A thin curved shape of the Moon, seen just after a new Moon or before one.
cards.say: crescent. A thin curved shape of the Moon, seen just after a new Moon or before one.

cards.back: An imaginary line through the North and South Poles that Earth spins around.
cards.say: axis. An imaginary line through the North and South Poles that Earth spins around.

cards.front: How much is Earth's axis tilted?
cards.back: About 23.5 degrees.
cards.say: How much is Earth's axis tilted? About twenty three point five degrees.

cards.back: Earth's axis is tilted, so different parts of Earth lean towards the Sun at different times of the year.
cards.say: Why do we have seasons? Earth's axis is tilted, so different parts of Earth lean towards the Sun at different times of the year.

cards.front: Why is it summer in the half of Earth tilted towards the Sun?
cards.back: The Sun is higher in the sky, days are longer and sunlight is more concentrated.
cards.say: Why is it summer in the half of Earth tilted towards the Sun? The Sun is higher in the sky, days are longer and sunlight is more concentrated.

cards.front: Why do countries near the equator have little change in seasons?
cards.back: They get strong sunlight and similar day lengths all year.
cards.say: Why do countries near the equator have little change in seasons? They get strong sunlight and similar day lengths all year.

cards.back: When the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun's light. Never look at the Sun, even during an eclipse.
cards.say: solar eclipse. When the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun's light. Never look at the Sun, even during an eclipse.

cards.back: An object that orbits a planet. The Moon is a natural satellite.
cards.say: satellite. An object that orbits a planet. The Moon is a natural satellite.
